command.roadweaver.mapaccess.allow.uncha: These players already have map access: %s
command.roadweaver.mapaccess.deny.unchan: These players are not in the map access list: %s
command.roadweaver.mapaccess.mode.ops_on: OPs and explicitly allowed players only
config.roadweaver.allow_artificial.toolt: If enabled, the mod will pave road surfaces. Disable to prevent paving (useful for planning or markers only).
config.roadweaver.allow_natural.tooltip: If enabled, the mod will pave natural road surfaces. Disable to prevent paving (useful for planning or markers only).
config.roadweaver.auto_mountain_threshol: Terrain profile AUTO only: when at least this fraction of a route is mountain terrain, that route uses tunnel-first grading (cut max 3) and the 3D height-aware search. Explicit profile modes ignore this.
config.roadweaver.auto_water_threshold_f: Terrain profile AUTO only: when at least this fraction of a route is water (river/lake/ocean), that route uses bridge-first grading (fill max 1) and relaxes the bridge depth threshold to 1. Explicit profile modes ignore this.
config.roadweaver.averaging_radius.toolt: Average height samples across N neighboring segments to reduce noise before smoothing.
config.roadweaver.biome_prefilter.toolti: Prefilter by allowed biomes of selected structures to reduce false positives and checks.
config.roadweaver.biome_weight.tooltip: Scales the cost difference between water and land. Set to 0 to disable this routing preference.
config.roadweaver.bridge_enabled.tooltip: Build elevated decks over water spans identified by the path analyzer.
config.roadweaver.bridge_max_length_bloc: If a water span is longer than this value, the entire span will be skipped (no bridge and no road). Set to 0 for unlimited.
config.roadweaver.bridge_merge_gap.toolt: Merge nearby bridge spans whose gap is at most this many segments to avoid frequent up-and-down decks over small islands or sand bars.
config.roadweaver.bridge_min_water_depth: Only build bridges over water columns whose depth (sea level minus ocean floor) is at least this many blocks. Helps ignore shallow puddles. Forced to 1 (ignored) in the BRIDGE_FIRST terrain mode.
config.roadweaver.bridge_share_radius.to:
When two different roads cross the same water within this distance they count as one crossing: the later road no longer builds its own bridge and reuses the earlier deck and deck height instead, joining the network at both ends.
Default 24, range 0-96. Set to 0 to disable sharing (every road builds its own bridge again).
config.roadweaver.bridge_pier_interval.t: Place supporting piers every N segments along the bridge.
config.roadweaver.bridge_pier_max_height: Stop extending a pier downward once this height is reached.
config.roadweaver.bridge_pier_width.tool: Square cross-section width for each pier (1-3).
config.roadweaver.bridge_ramp_segments.t: Number of segments used to smoothly ramp from ground height to deck height at both bridge ends.
config.roadweaver.bridge_use_buoys_inste: If enabled, place buoys on water spans instead of building a bridge.
config.roadweaver.bridge_use_buoys_when_: Use Buoys When Bridge Is Skipped
If enabled, when a bridge span is skipped due to exceeding max length, buoys will be placed on that span instead.
config.roadweaver.buoy_interval_blocks.t: Distance between buoys along a water span.
config.roadweaver.coarse_height_aware_en: When a coarse route has an unbuildable cliff, run the 3D height-aware candidate that can tunnel through or contour around the mountain.
config.roadweaver.coast_detour_multiplie: Allowed route length multiplier around coasts.
config.roadweaver.deviation_weight.toolt: Weight for deviation from a straight line. Higher values prefer straighter paths.
config.roadweaver.hard_grade_limit.toolt: Add hard cost for rise exceeding this grade when comparing climbs with tunnels. Must be at least the soft threshold; does not forbid travel.
config.roadweaver.hard_grade_penalty: Tunnel costing: hard grade excess cost
config.roadweaver.hard_grade_penalty.too: Multiply rise above the hard grade allowance by this unit cost, in addition to soft cost; not a ratio divided by the threshold.
config.roadweaver.biome_cost_water.toolt: A higher cost than land favors going around water or making a shorter crossing. Necessary crossings are still allowed.
config.roadweaver.biome_cost_other.toolt: Compared with water cost. Equal costs disable the preference. Specific land biomes are not scored.
config.roadweaver.soft_grade_limit.toolt: When comparing surface climbs with tunnels, charge soft cost for rise exceeding this grade; not a BAND passability limit.
config.roadweaver.soft_grade_penalty: Tunnel costing: soft grade excess cost
config.roadweaver.soft_grade_penalty.too: Multiply rise above the soft grade allowance by this unit cost; add hard excess cost to compare surface climbs with tunnels.
config.roadweaver.braid_min_direction_do: Two side-by-side roads with direction dot product at or above this count as parallel (mergeable). Below it they are crossings (T/X junction).
config.roadweaver.braid_near_parallel_do: Direction dot product in [parallel threshold, this value] is the near-parallel danger zone (a braid when not merged).
config.roadweaver.braid_allow_parallel_o: When off, two near-parallel roads may not overlap side-by-side (no braid). Default off.
config.roadweaver.diag_step_cost.tooltip: Diagonal step cost for local terrain repair; combines with orthogonal cost to shape repairs, not BAND/FMM.
config.roadweaver.dry_depression_bridge_: A land valley deeper than this many blocks is bridged instead of filled. Lower values create more bridges on shallow dry dips.
config.roadweaver.dynamic_plan_enabled.t: Periodically plan around players as new structures enter the configured radius.
config.roadweaver.dynamic_plan_radius_ch: Radius around each player (in chunks) to include structures in planning.
config.roadweaver.dynamic_plan_stride_ch: Step size (in chunks) for triggering dynamic planning as players move; larger stride triggers less frequently.
config.roadweaver.elevation_weight.toolt: Height change cost for local terrain repair; higher values favor flatter ground. Does not directly control BAND metrics.
config.roadweaver.enable_lamp.tooltip: Place road lamps or markers at the configured interval.
config.roadweaver.enable_prediction.tool: Predict structure locations based on world seed, filtered by whitelist/blacklist.
config.roadweaver.filter_unknown_endpoin:
Filter out connections whose unknown endpoint lies inside a village box (default ON), reducing pointless roads.
OFF = restore the old behavior.
config.roadweaver.gameplay_thread_cap.to:
Maximum threads road planning may use during ordinary gameplay (default 2; shared by structure resolution and coarse sampling).
Lower = less CPU, smoother play, slower road generation; 4~8 = faster generation but may stutter; 0 = unlimited (old behavior).
Note: gameplay only. Idle, Chunky prewarm and initial generation are never capped (they run at full speed).
Measured background: structure resolution was the biggest CPU consumer during gameplay (1735s cumulative), which easily saturated the CPU once rendering was added.
config.roadweaver.gpu_budget_free_fracti:
Fraction of currently-free VRAM RoadWeaver may use (default 0.70).
Lower = more conservative, less likely to collide (try ~0.5 on low-VRAM cards); higher = faster but may fill VRAM.
Note: this only throttles when a single batch is very large - see the next entry.
config.roadweaver.gpu_budget_hard_cap_mi:
Hard cap on VRAM used by one batch (default 4096 MiB). 0 = uncapped (not recommended).
Important: single batches in this modpack are small (~97 MiB), so this cap only starts to bite when lowered to roughly 128~256.
Otherwise lowering it has no observable effect - that is not a bug, the limit simply is not being reached.
config.roadweaver.grade_repair_paralleli: Threads for the local grade-repair window pool. 0 = auto (scaled to CPU count and road-worker budget, never below 4). The old fixed 4-thread pool left most road workers blocked while cores idled.
config.roadweaver.grade_repair_window_st: Base A* state ceiling for one local grade-repair window (default 90000, the historical value). Lower it on slower machines to trade repair ambition for latency; tunnel windows may still scale above it.
config.roadweaver.height_anomaly_detour_:
Largest detour window for construction height conflicts (default 96, range 16~512).
Higher = climbing sections are likelier to find a bypass, but slower.
config.roadweaver.height_aware_state_lim: Maximum expanded states for the expensive 3D height-aware coarse candidate. Lower is faster but may fail on long mountain routes.
config.roadweaver.height_repair_context_: Length of route context kept on each side of a height conflict during local repair.
config.roadweaver.height_tunnel_threshol: A vertical change above this many blocks is treated as a tunnel candidate instead of a normal surface cut.
config.roadweaver.heuristic_weight.toolt: Heuristic multiplier for local terrain repair search. Values above 1 favor the goal without optimality guarantees; does not control BAND/FMM.
config.roadweaver.idle_concurrent_genera: Maximum low-priority idle road tasks in flight. This is separate from normal road concurrency but remains subject to the total runtime task budget and external QoS.
config.roadweaver.idle_generation_enable: When enabled, RoadWeaver continues expanding and generating roads near players at the lowest normal-worker priority.
config.roadweaver.idle_thread_duty_cycle: CPU duty cycle for low-priority idle generation tasks (1-100%). Default 20%. Lower values save CPU but generate idle roads slower.
config.roadweaver.initial_generation_thr:
Worker threads used during initial world generation. 0 = derive from hardware and memory.
WARNING: this value is read once when the server starts and then cached - you MUST reopen the save (or restart the game) for changes to take effect. Editing it in this menu does nothing immediately.
config.roadweaver.initial_plan_radius_ch: At new world start, build network around spawn within this radius (in chunks).
config.roadweaver.lake_detour_multiplier: Allowed route length multiplier around lakes.
config.roadweaver.lake_detour_radius_max: Largest lake-detour radius attempted around a water conflict.
config.roadweaver.lamp_interval.tooltip: Place roadside lamps by accumulated route distance in blocks.
config.roadweaver.large_structure_offset: Distance from road center for large structures in blocks.
config.roadweaver.loading_progress_enabl: Show RoadWeaver generation progress information on the world loading screen.
config.roadweaver.loading_tips_enabled.t: Show RoadWeaver related tips and tricks in the bottom right corner of the world loading screen.
config.roadweaver.local_conflict_radius_: Radius of the conflict-centred circle used by local route repair. Larger radii can resolve more but cost more sampling.
config.roadweaver.local_repair_only_on_u: When true (default) a building-protected-gap route goes through the local-repair wave. When false the gap route is kept as-is right after the initial batch and the local-repair wave is skipped — faster on gap-heavy batches, but local detours are not attempted. Reverting restores the prior behavior.
config.roadweaver.local_repair_window_cl:
Radius within which nearby gaps are merged into one repair (default 50).
Higher = more gaps merged, lower total cost; 0 = restore the old padding/4 behavior.
Too high can make a single window so large that it becomes slower.
config.roadweaver.max_concurrent_generat: Maximum normal road tasks after entering a world. It is also the shared runtime safety-slot ceiling for normal and idle roads; it does not affect startup generation.
config.roadweaver.max_grade_fraction.too:
Maximum vertical change allowed per block of horizontal travel (default 0.5, range 0.1~0.9).
Lower = flatter (may detour or tunnel more); higher = straighter but steeper.
Above 0.6 is not recommended - steep grades noticeably hurt how roads look and how they get paved.
config.roadweaver.max_slope_step_per_two: Maximum Y change allowed across 2 segments when slope limiting is enabled.
config.roadweaver.max_structures_per_roa: Maximum number of roadside structures to place per road. Set to 0 to disable structures.
config.roadweaver.medium_structure_offse: Distance from road center for medium structures (e.g., coffee houses) in blocks.
Minimum distance between roadside structures in blocks. Larger values result in sparser distribution.
config.roadweaver.mountain_detour_multip: Allowed route length multiplier for mountain detours.
config.roadweaver.mountain_overburden_bl: Terrain above the road by at least this many blocks marks a station as mountain, preferred for a tunnel or switchback.
config.roadweaver.mountain_surface_cut.t: Maximum ordinary-road cut on mountain stations.
Maximum ordinary-road fill on mountain stations.
config.roadweaver.near_water_cost.toolti: Cost for being near water. Higher values prefer to stay away from water.
config.roadweaver.ocean_detour_multiplie: Allowed route length multiplier around ocean crossings.
Probability that a long ocean crossing becomes an undersea tunnel instead of a bridge.
config.roadweaver.opencl_accurate_sampli:
WARNING: this switch does NOTHING in the current version.
Accurate height sampling has intentionally been CPU-only since 0.8.340 (the modpack's terrain noise is too complex; a single GPU buffer does not fit and every request fell back to CPU anyway).
Kept only so the config entry is not lost. For coarse-sampling GPU options see "Runtime GPU Policy".
config.roadweaver.opencl_coarse_gpu_conc: Maximum number of concurrent coarse-sampling requests RoadWeaver may run on the GPU during normal gameplay. It is a request count, not a fixed percentage. 0 = automatic (the runtime picks the safe lane count from GPU memory and foreground pressure). 1 = only one lane ever, the most conservative choice that leaves the GPU almost entirely to the game. 2-4 = balanced: still keeps headroom for rendering while sampling noticeably faster. Higher = more throughput but can steal GPU time from the game. Startup prewarm, Chunky prewarm, active Chunky, Streams, C2ME and rendering are never limited by this value.
config.roadweaver.opencl_coarse_sampling: When enabled, coarse terrain height sampling prefers OpenCL acceleration and falls back to CPU if unavailable or failed. When disabled, CPU is always used.
config.roadweaver.opencl_device_preferen: Select the OpenCL device type for coarse height sampling. AUTO prefers GPU first, then CPU OpenCL.
config.roadweaver.opencl_min_samples.too: Only try OpenCL when one coarse height request reaches this many samples. 0 means every coarse tile can try OpenCL.
config.roadweaver.opencl_validate_sample: When enabled, representative samples from every coarse and accurate OpenCL request are checked against CPU output. A mismatch disables only the affected program and falls back to CPU. Debug option with high overhead.
config.roadweaver.ortho_step_cost.toolti: Orthogonal step cost for local terrain repair; also sets baseline surface cost in tunnel comparisons.
config.roadweaver.other_structure_road_o: Distance (in blocks) from road endpoints to non-village structure centers.
config.roadweaver.pass_through_village_c:
Clip the village bounding boxes a road passes through so it does not cut into the village (default ON).
OFF = restore the old behavior.
config.roadweaver.pathfinding_parallel_w:
How the main thread waits for the per-road searches during coarse planning.
OFF (default): wait one by one - bit-for-bit identical to older versions.
ON: wait for all to finish together. Semantically equivalent; revert to OFF if anything looks wrong.
Note: tasks already enter one thread pool in submission order, so both waiting styles take the SAME total time mathematically - expect no perceptible difference.
config.roadweaver.pause_coarse_gpu_while: Yield GPU while the map is open

ON (default): while the RoadWeaver map is open, GPU coarse sampling pauses so map rendering gets the GPU to itself - opening the map no longer stutters. Sampling resumes the moment you close it.\nOFF: the map and sampling fight over the same GPU, which measurably stutters the map (especially with large sampling regions).\nApplies immediately.
Yield GPU while any screen is open

ON (default): while the inventory, pause menu, a furnace/crafting table or any other screen is open, GPU coarse sampling pauses so the interface stays responsive. Opening a screen does not send a server interaction packet, so the older yield rules never fired for it - which is why the inventory and ESC could stutter. Sampling resumes the moment you close the screen.
The chat screen is included too (0.8.351: it used to be excluded, but that still stuttered).
OFF: only the map gate applies.
config.roadweaver.plain_surface_cut.tool: Maximum ordinary-road cut on flat terrain.
config.roadweaver.plain_surface_fill.too: Maximum ordinary-road fill on flat terrain.
config.roadweaver.component_min_angle_de:
When joining disconnected network components, the minimum angle between two edges from the same structure (default 35°).
Changing it alters the planning fingerprint and recomputes cached routes.
config.roadweaver.component_degree_cap: Component Join Max Edges per Node
config.roadweaver.component_degree_cap.t:
When joining components, the maximum number of edges a structure may have (default 3).
Changing it alters the planning fingerprint and recomputes cached routes.
config.roadweaver.plan_max_edge_len_bloc:
Maximum distance for two structures to be connected directly (default 2048). Beyond it they are not linked directly; the bridging stage may still join them.
Higher: allow farther structures to connect directly. Lower: only connect nearby ones.
Changing it alters the planning fingerprint and recomputes cached routes (decide before creating a world).
config.roadweaver.bridge_join_len_blocks:
When the network splits into components, two components are bridged only if their closest points are within this distance (default 1536).
Higher: distant villages also join the network (more connected, longer total length). Lower: a more fragmented network.
Changing it alters the planning fingerprint and recomputes cached routes (decide before creating a world).
config.roadweaver.attach_to_existing_roa: Attach failed routes to nearby roads (radius)

When A* finds no usable route at all, search this radius around both endpoints for an existing road and re-generate with the endpoint moved onto that road (produces a short connector). 0 disables. Measured: three failed connections were only 0-64 blocks away from existing roads.
config.roadweaver.prefer_unsmoothed_on_p: Prefer unsmoothed route when a gap appears

When smoothing leaves a protection gap, also compute the unsmoothed route and pick the better one (default ON).
Reduces "road surface cut by a building", at the cost of a few slightly rigid stretches. OFF = old behavior.
config.roadweaver.prefilter_structure_st:
Skip candidate chunks that are provably empty (default ON). Saves time only, never changes results.
OFF = old behavior (slower).
When enabled, trees and large plants (bamboo, huge fungi) will not generate on or near roads. This prevents floating trees caused by road cutting.
config.roadweaver.radius_chunks.tooltip: Prediction radius centered at spawn, in chunks.
config.roadweaver.river_detour_multiplie: Allowed route length multiplier around rivers.
config.roadweaver.river_repair_bypass_pr:
Detect doomed river local searches up front and skip them (default ON). Saves time only, never changes results.
OFF = old behavior (slower).
config.roadweaver.road_clear_height.tool: Vertical space cleared above the road surface in non-tunnel mode. Higher values carve more headroom but may cut into nearby terrain or structures.
config.roadweaver.road_signs_enabled.too: When enabled, place distance signs near both ends of a road and place warning signs when an over-long sea crossing is skipped.
config.roadweaver.roads_enabled.tooltip: Master switch for the road system. When disabled, road planning/generation and feature placement will be skipped.
config.roadweaver.roadside_structures_en: When enabled, decorative structures (benches, campfires, coffee houses) will be placed along roads based on biome and road length.
config.roadweaver.roadside_village_build: Spacing between adjacent buildings (default 3, range 2~8). Lower = more compact.
config.roadweaver.roadside_village_enabl: When enabled, generate clustered village pieces along suitable road sections.
config.roadweaver.roadside_village_max_c:
Largest curve angle allowed (default 70, range 0~180).
Higher = more stretches qualify; must be >= the minimum angle above.
config.roadweaver.roadside_village_max_d:
How far a node may sit from the village center (default 96, range 16~128).
Higher = more spread-out villages.
config.roadweaver.roadside_village_max_h:
Maximum height difference allowed within a village (default 4, range 0~12).
Higher = allow more rugged terrain (may look worse).
config.roadweaver.roadside_village_max_l:
Maximum local slope allowed (default 4, range 0~8).
Higher = copes with steeper terrain, at the cost of a less level village.
config.roadweaver.roadside_village_max_p: Maximum number of roadside village clusters to precompute for each generated road. Higher values make villages more frequent.
config.roadweaver.roadside_village_max_s: Largest height step allowed between adjacent plots (default 3, range 1~6). Lower = flatter.
config.roadweaver.roadside_village_min_c: Smallest curve angle required for a site (default 0, range 0~180). Higher = prefer bends.
config.roadweaver.roadside_village_min_r:
A road must be at least this long before a roadside village is considered (default 32, range 32~512).
Higher = only long roads get villages.
config.roadweaver.roadside_village_node_:
Most nodes a single village generates (default 14, range 1~24).
Higher = larger, denser villages that occupy more terrain.
Fewest nodes a single village generates (default 6, range 1~24).
config.roadweaver.roadside_village_road_:
Distance kept between the village and the road (default 6, range 4~64).
Higher = further from the road (never blocks it); lower = more compact; too low blocks the road.
config.roadweaver.roadside_village_spawn: Probability for each road to generate a roadside village. 0.3 means 30% of roads will have villages.
config.roadweaver.roadside_village_windo:
Length of the candidate stretch evaluated per attempt (default 24, range 24~256).
Higher = longer candidates but slower evaluation.
config.roadweaver.runtime_coarse_gpu_act:
Minimum gap between two GPU coarse batches while you are moving or interacting (default 1500).
Higher = more conservative, fewer stutters, slower generation; lower = faster but more likely to stutter; 0 = unlimited (not recommended).
Separate from the idle setting. Applies immediately.
config.roadweaver.runtime_coarse_gpu_min:
Minimum gap between two GPU coarse batches while you are idle (default 1500).
Higher = quieter background; lower = faster idle generation; 0 = unlimited. Applies immediately.
config.roadweaver.runtime_coarse_max_thr:
Maximum concurrent GPU coarse requests while idle (default 2).
Higher = faster idle generation but more GPU usage; 1 = most conservative; 0 = auto-detect from hardware. Applies within 1 second.
config.roadweaver.runtime_coarse_min_thr:
GPU coarse lanes always reserved during Chunky / foreground pressure (default 1).
Keep at 1 on low-end machines: background still progresses slowly without stuttering while you play. Applies within 1 second.
config.roadweaver.runtime_coarse_use_cpu: Use CPU for coarse sampling during gameplay

ON (default): coarse sampling uses CPU while you play, so the GPU never competes with rendering - steadier frame rate, but noticeably slower road generation.
OFF: gameplay also uses the GPU - faster planning, but a low-end GPU may stutter briefly (if it still stutters, raise "Active GPU submit interval").
Applies immediately.
config.roadweaver.runtime_road_completio:
How long to wait after a road completes before planning the next one (default 1500).
Higher = roads trickle in one by one, almost unnoticeable in play; lower = continuous generation, more likely to stutter; 0 = unlimited. Applies immediately.
config.roadweaver.sampling_in_flight_tim: How long a road worker may wait for another thread's in-flight coarse/accurate sampling job before taking the job over or failing that request. Prevents permanent stalls when a sampling thread hangs.
Shared worker threads during gameplay. 0 = derive from hardware.
WARNING - two limits apply: (1) the effective cap is min(12, CPU cores - 2); larger values are ignored. (2) While you move or interact, foreground protection forces this down to 2 (and to 1 under HyperSpeed cruise protection) - raising it has no effect then.
Changes are hot-applied within about one second; no need to reopen the save.
config.roadweaver.slope_limit_enabled.to: When enabled, the road height profile will be smoothed by limiting steep slopes.
config.roadweaver.small_structure_offset: Distance from road center for small structures (e.g., benches, campfires) in blocks.
config.roadweaver.spawn_cabin_enabled: Enable connection to spawn point road
config.roadweaver.spawn_cabin_enabled.to: Connect the road from the spawn point to the surrounding structures.
config.roadweaver.stability_weight.toolt: Weight for terrain stability. Higher values avoid cliffs and pits.
config.roadweaver.structure_avoidance_en: When enabled, roads will automatically skip segments that fall within structure bounding boxes (e.g., village buildings), preventing roads from damaging structures.
config.roadweaver.structure_detour_radiu: Largest building-detour radius attempted before retaining a protected gap.
Smallest building-detour radius attempted around a structure conflict.
Radius increment between successive building-detour attempts.
Distance (in blocks) from road endpoints to structure centers. Roads will start/end this far from village centers.
config.roadweaver.structure_selection.no: No structure data found. Please enter a world first to discover structures.
config.roadweaver.surface_cut_max_blocks: Maximum the road surface may be cut below terrain for a normal road. Higher values allow deeper trenches; keep low to prefer tunnels/bridges on big hills.
config.roadweaver.surface_fill_max_block: Maximum the road surface may be raised above terrain on a normal road. Keep low to avoid filling lakes and deep valleys.
config.roadweaver.switchback_strength.to: How willing mountain planning is to use longer winding switchbacks. Higher = more curves and longer detours; lower = closer to direct contours and tunnels.
config.roadweaver.terrain_profile_mode.t: Auto is the balanced baseline (legacy 'Balanced' saves load as Auto). Tunnel First tightens cut to 3 and also runs the 3D height-aware search on mountain routes; Bridge First tightens fill to 1 and lets water crossings ignore the bridge depth threshold; Light Cut only tightens cut (max 3) and fill (max 1) — it does not change any search behavior.
Choose the road pathfinding mode. Legacy Direct does not build a large coarse terrain region; Coarse + Corridor refines only the active path corridor. Full Region requires a validated FP64 GPU and may safely downgrade for the current world session.
config.roadweaver.thread_duty_cycle.tool: CPU usage ratio for worker threads (1-100%). 100% = full speed; 50% = work 20ms then rest 20ms, etc. Lower values reduce CPU load but slow down road generation.
config.roadweaver.title: RoadWeaver Configuration
config.roadweaver.tunnel_clear_height.to:
Interior clearance of tunnels (default 5, range 2~16).
Higher = roomier tunnels but much more digging. Requires "Enable tunnel clearance" above.
config.roadweaver.tunnel_depth_blocks.to: Maximum depth the coarse/repair profile may lower a sustained mountain hump into a tunnel chord.
config.roadweaver.tunnel_enabled.tooltip:
Whether to carve tunnel ceilings to a clearance height (default OFF = use road clearance).
When enabled, also set the tunnel clearance height below.
config.roadweaver.tunnel_min_run.tooltip: A tunnel run must contain at least this many consecutive stations to be kept as a tunnel.
config.roadweaver.village_road_offset.to: Distance (in blocks) from road endpoints to village centers. Roads will start/end this far from villages.
config.roadweaver.water_depth_weight.too: Weight for water depth. Higher values avoid deep water.

config.roadweaver.tunnel_dry_seal: Dry sealed tunnel (keep water out of the bore)
config.roadweaver.tunnel_dry_seal.toolti: After carving, dry the bore and replace the water that touches the lining with stone, so no water hangs inside the tunnel. On by default; portals are only dried, never walled off.
config.roadweaver.culvert_enabled: Narrow streams cross on a culvert
config.roadweaver.culvert_enabled.toolti: A narrow, shallow stream is neither filled into a dam nor skipped: the deck is lifted above the water so the stream keeps flowing underneath. On by default.
config.roadweaver.culvert_max_stations.t: Wider watercourses are left to a bridge, instead of a culvert carved into the middle of a river. Default 6.
config.roadweaver.culvert_max_water_dept: Deeper water needs thicker walls than a culvert carries, so it is left to a bridge. Default 2.
config.roadweaver.slope_by_arc_length: Measure slopes by real arc length
config.roadweaver.slope_by_arc_length.to: A diagonal station is sqrt(2) blocks from its predecessor, so a per-station limit makes the same road steeper on diagonals. On, the limit follows the real distance (it only ever relaxes a long edge; off is bit-for-bit the old behaviour). Off by default - compare both ways on the same area first.
config.roadweaver.path_grid_step.tooltip: Sampling spacing for BAND/Fast Marching and local terrain repair. Larger spacing means fewer samples and coarser detail; it does not set road width or final station spacing.
Pathfinding: BAND (Finsler metric + Fast Marching + elastic band).
